en: join in; help; assist; lend a hand to an effort

examples.en: My friends joined in on the cleaning too.
The wind joined in, so it felt even colder.

examples.ko: 우리 팀을 응원하는 사람들이 점점 가세해요.
examples.en: More and more people are joining in to cheer for our team.
My father will lend a hand with this too.

examples.ko: 비까지 가세한 날이라 길이 많이 막혔어요.
examples.en: With rain on top of everything, the roads were badly jammed.

examples.ko: 이웃 사람들이 가세하자 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Once the neighbors pitched in, the work finished quickly.

explain: '돕다'는 어떤 상황에서든 쓰지만 '가세하다'는 이미 진행 중인 일이나 싸움에 힘을 보태러 끼어드는 느낌이에요. '~에 가세하다'로 쓰고, '악재가 가세하다'처럼 나쁜 일이 겹칠 때도 써요.
explain_en: Unlike the all-purpose 돕다, 가세하다 means stepping into something already under way to add your weight to it. It takes 에 ('~에 가세하다'), and bad factors can also 'join in', as in '악재가 가세하다'.

examples.en: The company officially disclosed this year's results.
City Hall posts the new rules officially on its website.
The bank will publicly announce its interest rates every month.
The date for publicly announcing the results has been set.
That information hasn't been officially disclosed yet.

examples.ko: 법에 따라 회사는 중요한 내용을 공시해야 해요.
examples.en: By law, a company has to disclose important information publicly.

explain: '발표하다'는 누구나 쓰지만 '공시하다'는 회사나 관청이 규칙에 따라 공식적으로 알릴 때 써요. 경제 뉴스나 기업 보고서에서 많이 보고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: 발표하다 works for anyone, but 공시하다 is for a company or government office announcing something officially, following rules. You see it in business news and reports, almost never in daily conversation.

en: stand out; come into the spotlight; be brought into relief

examples.ko: 이 문제가 요즘 크게 부각되고 있어요.
examples.en: This issue has come into the spotlight a lot these days.

examples.ko: 그 배우의 연기가 영화에서 가장 부각됐어요.
examples.en: That actor's performance stood out the most in the movie.
New strengths will gradually come to the fore.

examples.ko: 색이 어두워서 글자가 잘 부각되지 않아요.
examples.en: The color is dark, so the letters don't stand out well.

examples.ko: 사고가 난 뒤에 안전 문제가 부각되었어요.
examples.en: After the accident, the safety issue came into focus.
Please check once more the problems that are coming to the fore.

explain: '눈에 띄다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '부각되다'는 뉴스나 발표에서 문제나 장점이 주목받을 때 많이 써요. 사람이 실력으로 눈에 띌 때는 '두각을 나타내다'가 더 자연스러워요. 일부러 강조할 때는 '부각시키다'를 써요.
explain_en: 눈에 띄다 is the everyday phrase; 부각되다 is common in news and presentations when a problem or strength gets attention. For a person who stands out through skill, '두각을 나타내다' sounds more natural. When you emphasize something on purpose, use '부각시키다'.

examples.en: This award is a great honor for me.
He won the glory of victory.
The honor went to all of the players.

examples.ko: 이런 영예가 저에게 올 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I never thought such an honor would come to me.

examples.ko: 영예와 책임은 항상 함께 오는 법이에요.
examples.en: Honor and responsibility always come together.

examples.ko: 그녀는 오랜 노력 끝에 영예의 자리에 올랐어요.
examples.en: After long effort, she rose to a place of honor.

explain: '명예'와 비슷하지만 '영예'는 큰 상이나 업적처럼 빛나는 일을 얻었을 때의 자랑스러움에 가까워요. '영예를 안다', '영예를 얻다'처럼 쓰고, 말보다 글이나 시상식 연설에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Close to 명예, but 영예 is the proud, shining feeling of earning something big like a major prize or achievement. It pairs with '영예를 안다' and '영예를 얻다', and shows up more in writing and award speeches than in casual talk.

examples.ko: 이 자리에 서게 되어 정말 영예로워요.
examples.en: I'm truly honored to stand here.
I'm happy to receive such an honorable award.

examples.ko: 그 일은 우리 가족에게 정말 영예로웠어요.
examples.en: That was a real honor for our family.
I want to retire with honor.

examples.ko: 대표로 뽑힌 일이 정말 영예로울 거예요.
examples.en: Being chosen as the representative will be a real honor.

examples.ko: 너무 영예로워서 말이 잘 안 나와요.
examples.en: I'm so honored that I can hardly speak.

explain: ㅂ 불규칙이라 '영예로워요', '영예로운'으로 바뀌어요. 상이나 높은 자리를 받은 일에 써서 '영광스럽다'와 비슷하게 쓰고, 공식적인 자리에서 많이 들어요.
explain_en: It's a ㅂ-irregular adjective: 영예로워요, 영예로운. You use it for receiving an award or high position, much like 영광스럽다, and you hear it mostly on formal occasions.

en: guarantee; assure; vouch for; swear confidently

examples.en: I swear I'll pass this exam.
Nobody can guarantee the result.
He said so with full confidence.

examples.ko: 내일 비가 안 올 거라고 장담하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to be sure it won't rain tomorrow.
My friend vouched that it was delicious and took me to the restaurant.
Don't be so quick to say you're sure.

explain: '약속하다'는 앞으로 하겠다고 정하는 것이고, '장담하다'는 틀림없다고 자신 있게 말하는 거예요. 그래서 '장담할 수 없다', '장담하기 어렵다'처럼 부정형으로 자주 써요.
explain_en: 약속하다 commits you to doing something; 장담하다 is saying with confidence that something is certain. That's why it often appears in negative forms like '장담할 수 없다' and '장담하기 어렵다'.

examples.en: The pharmacist made up my cold medicine.
They prepare the medicine according to the prescription.
The herbal doctor is preparing the herbal medicine.

examples.ko: 약을 조제하는 데 십 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about ten minutes to prepare the medicine.

examples.ko: 이 약은 약국에서만 조제할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can only be made up at a pharmacy.

examples.ko: 어제 조제한 약을 아직 안 먹었어요.
examples.en: I haven't taken the medicine that was prepared yesterday.

explain: '만들다'와 달리 약을 처방에 맞게 섞어 만들 때 써요. 약국에서 '조제해 드릴게요'라는 말을 자주 들어요. 음식에는 거의 쓰지 않고 '만들다'를 써요.
explain_en: Unlike 만들다, 조제하다 is for mixing and making up medicine to match a prescription. At a pharmacy you often hear '조제해 드릴게요'. For food, people almost always say 만들다 instead.

examples.ko: 영화에서 총격 장면이 나오자 아이가 눈을 가렸어요.
examples.en: When a gunfight scene came up in the movie, the child covered his eyes.
When the gunfire stopped, people came outside.

examples.ko: 게임 속에서 총격을 받고 캐릭터가 쓰러졌어요.
examples.en: In the game, my character was shot at and fell down.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 총격 장면이 너무 많아서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: That movie has too many shooting scenes, so it was scary.
A long gunfight broke out at the end of the movie.

examples.ko: 영화 속 총격 소리에 놀란 아이가 울기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The child, startled by the gunfire in the movie, began to cry.

explain: '총소리'는 소리 자체를 말하고, '총격'은 총을 쏘는 행위나 사건을 가리켜요. 뉴스에서 '총격 사건', '총격을 받다', '총격전'처럼 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: 총소리 is the sound of a gun; 총격 is the act or incident of shooting. In the news you see '총격 사건', '총격을 받다', and '총격전' a lot, but it's rare in daily conversation.

en: step down; resign from a position

examples.en: The president took responsibility and stepped down.
The coach will step down when the season ends.
People are demanding that the CEO step down.
I hear the chairman will step down within this year.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 끝까지 퇴진하지 않겠다고 말했어요.
examples.en: That lawmaker said they would not step down no matter what.
Nobody knew why they were suddenly stepping down.

explain: '그만두다'는 누구에게나 쓰지만 '퇴진하다'는 사장, 감독, 대표처럼 높은 자리에서 물러날 때 써요. 일반 직원이나 학생에게는 어색해요. 뉴스에서 '퇴진을 요구하다'로 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 그만두다 works for anyone, but 퇴진하다 is for leaving a high post such as president, coach, or CEO. It sounds odd for an ordinary employee or student. In the news you often see '퇴진을 요구하다'.

en: pour in all at once; surge; (vehicle) speed recklessly

examples.en: Applications for the event poured in all at once.
Orders flooded in, so packing got very delayed.
When visitors surge, the site slows down.
Calls with questions will flood in tomorrow.
I woke up to the sound of a motorcycle racing recklessly.
Requests are pouring in, so the server is shaky.

explain: '주문이 폭주하다', '접속이 폭주하다'처럼 한꺼번에 너무 많이 몰릴 때 써요. 또 차나 오토바이가 위험하게 마구 달릴 때도 써요. 주어는 주문, 신청, 문의 같은 말이 많아요.
explain_en: Used when too much arrives at once, as in '주문이 폭주하다' or '접속이 폭주하다'. It also describes a car or motorcycle racing dangerously. Typical subjects are 주문, 신청, and 문의.

en: be imprinted (in one's mind); be etched

examples.ko: 그 장면이 제 머릿속에 깊이 각인됐어요.
examples.en: That scene got deeply etched in my mind.
First impressions tend to stay imprinted for a long time.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 들은 말이 마음에 각인될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Words you hear as a child can get imprinted on your heart.
The brand name has been firmly imprinted in people's minds.

examples.ko: 그날의 기억은 지금도 선명하게 각인되어 있어요.
examples.en: The memory of that day is still vividly etched in me.
We chose a short name so that it would stick in people's minds.

explain: '기억에 남다'는 편하게 쓰는 말이고, '각인되다'는 도장을 찍은 듯 깊이 박혀 지워지지 않는 느낌이에요. '머릿속에', '마음에', '사람들에게'와 함께 쓰고, 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 기억에 남다 is the casual option; 각인되다 feels like something stamped in so deeply it won't wear off. It goes with '머릿속에', '마음에', or '사람들에게', and appears more in writing and presentations.

examples.en: The player etched that defeat into their heart.
Be sure to engrave these words in your mind.
The students imprint the rules in their heads.

examples.ko: 브랜드 이름을 사람들에게 각인하려고 광고를 했어요.
examples.en: They ran ads to make the brand name stick with people.
I live with that day's promise engraved in me.
It was an experience impressive enough to etch in deeply.

explain: '각인되다'가 저절로 깊이 박히는 것이라면 '각인하다'는 일부러 새기는 거예요. '가슴에 각인하다', '마음에 각인하다'로 자주 써요. 일상 대화보다 글이나 연설에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: If 각인되다 means something gets imprinted by itself, 각인하다 means you imprint it on purpose. Common in '가슴에 각인하다' and '마음에 각인하다', and more at home in writing and speeches than in daily talk.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 아주 작은 균의 검출이 가능해요.
examples.en: This machine can detect even very tiny germs.
I'll let you know the test results tomorrow.

examples.ko: 검출을 쉽게 하려고 물에 색을 넣었어요.
examples.en: We added color to the water to make detection easier.

examples.ko: 새 프로그램은 오류 검출 속도가 훨씬 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: The new program is much faster at detecting errors.

examples.ko: 화재 때 연기 검출은 센서가 맡아요.
examples.en: In a fire, a sensor handles the smoke detection.
Detection failed, so we tested again yesterday.

explain: '찾아내다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '검출'은 기계나 검사 방법으로 어떤 것이 있는지 확인해 낼 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '성분이 검출되다'처럼 동사 '검출되다'로 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 찾아내다 is the everyday word; 검출 is for confirming through a machine or test that something is present. In the news the verb form appears more often, as in '성분이 검출되다'.

examples.ko: 올해 우리 회사의 매출이 예상을 상회했어요.
examples.en: This year our company's sales exceeded expectations.
Days with temperatures above the yearly average continue.

examples.ko: 수입이 지출을 상회하면 저축할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If income is above spending, you can save.

examples.ko: 이번 달 판매량이 목표를 상회할 거예요.
examples.en: This month's sales will exceed the target.
The number of participants is running above expectations.
My score didn't make it above the average.

explain: '넘다'보다 딱딱한 말이고, 숫자나 기준, 예상과 비교할 때 써요. 짝말은 '하회하다'(기준보다 낮다)예요. '예상을 상회하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 쓰고 뉴스나 경제 보고서에서 자주 봐요.
explain_en: A stiffer word than 넘다, used when comparing to numbers, standards, or expectations. Its opposite is 하회하다 (to fall below). It takes 을/를 as in '예상을 상회하다' and is common in news and business reports.

en: win an order; take on a contract

examples.en: Our company won a big construction contract.

examples.ko: 그 공장은 새 주문을 수주해서 바빠요.
examples.en: That factory is busy after taking on a new order.

examples.ko: 해외에서 배 열 척을 수주할 예정이에요.
examples.en: They plan to win an order for ten ships from overseas.

examples.ko: 큰 계약을 수주하는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Winning a big contract is not easy.

examples.ko: 건설사가 새 다리 공사를 수주하고 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: The construction firm was delighted to win the new bridge job.

examples.ko: 우리는 아직 그 공사를 수주하지 못했어요.
examples.en: We haven't won that construction job yet.

explain: 일을 맡는 쪽이 주문이나 공사를 받을 때 써요. 반대로 일을 맡기는 쪽은 '발주하다'예요. 건설이나 조선 회사 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: Used by the side that takes on the work, receiving an order or construction job. The side that hands out the work uses 발주하다. It shows up in news about construction and shipbuilding firms, and almost never in daily talk.

examples.en: They say loneliness is sometimes a writer's fate.
The two met again as if by destiny.
He accepted his fate and lived hard.
This may be our destiny.
The two countries are called fated rivals.

examples.ko: 그녀는 숙명에서 벗어나려고 먼 곳으로 떠났어요.
examples.en: She went far away to escape her fate.

explain: '운명'과 비슷하지만 '숙명'은 바꿀 수 없이 처음부터 정해진 느낌이 더 강해요. '숙명의 라이벌'처럼 이야기나 글에서 많이 쓰고, 보통 대화에서는 '운명'을 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Similar to 운명, but 숙명 feels more strongly like something fixed from the start that can't be changed. It's common in stories and writing, as in '숙명의 라이벌'; in plain conversation people use 운명 more.

examples.ko: 대통령은 이번 주에 지방 순회를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The president began a tour of the provinces this week.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 순회 공연이 다음 달에 시작돼요.
examples.en: That singer's touring concerts start next month.

examples.ko: 긴 순회 공연이 끝나고 가수는 오랜만에 집에 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: After the long tour, the singer came home for the first time in a while.
The guard makes rounds of the building every night.

examples.ko: 이번 순회에 참가한 학생이 모두 열 명이에요.
examples.en: Ten students in all took part in this tour.

examples.ko: 경비 순회는 하루에 두 번 있어요.
examples.en: The guard's rounds happen twice a day.

explain: '돌아다니다'는 목적 없이도 쓰지만 '순회'는 정해진 곳을 차례로 돌며 일을 하는 거예요. '순회 공연', '지방 순회', '순회 진료'처럼 다른 명사 앞에도 붙어요. 일상 대화보다 안내문이나 뉴스에서 봐요.
explain_en: 돌아다니다 can be aimless, but 순회 means going through set places in order to do a job. It also sits in front of other nouns, as in '순회 공연', '지방 순회', and '순회 진료'. You meet it in notices and news more than in conversation.

en: go around; go round; tour; make the rounds

examples.en: The teacher goes around the classroom helping students.
The nurse makes the rounds of the wards one by one.
The doctor went around the islands seeing patients.
This bus is a route that circles the tourist spots.
Our team plans to tour the whole country.
Who was the person who went around the village yesterday?

explain: 정해진 곳을 차례로 돌 때 써요. '돌아다니다'는 자유롭게 다니는 느낌이라 달라요. '순찰하다'는 경찰이나 경비가 안전을 살피러 돌 때 주로 쓰고, '순회하다'는 가르치거나 공연하거나 진료하러 돌 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used for going around set places in order. 돌아다니다 feels free and aimless, so it differs. 순찰하다 is mostly for police or guards checking safety, while 순회하다 also covers going around to teach, perform, or treat patients.

examples.en: We talked about human existence in philosophy class.

examples.ko: 그 인물의 실존 여부는 아직 확실하지 않아요.
examples.en: Whether that figure really existed is still unclear.

examples.ko: 실존이 본질에 앞선다는 말을 들어 봤어요?
examples.en: Have you heard the saying that existence precedes essence?

examples.ko: 이 책에서는 실존과 자유를 함께 다뤄요.
examples.en: This book deals with existence and freedom together.
Everyone has worries about existence.
Even now, existence is an important theme in philosophy.

explain: 일상에서 '존재'보다 좁게, '실존 인물', '실존 여부'처럼 실제로 있었는지를 말할 때 써요. 철학에서는 '실존주의'처럼 사람이 지금 여기에서 사는 상태를 말해요. 이야기 속에만 있는 인물은 '가상'이나 '허구'라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily use it is narrower than 존재, appearing in '실존 인물' and '실존 여부' when asking whether something really existed. In philosophy, as in '실존주의', it refers to a person's living here and now. A figure that only exists in stories is called 가상 or 허구.

examples.ko: 이 이야기 속 인물은 천 년 전에 실존했던 사람이에요.
examples.en: The person in this story is someone who really existed a thousand years ago.
Nobody believes dragons actually exist.
I debated with friends whether God really exists.

examples.ko: 이런 마을이 실존할 거라고 생각하지 못했어요.
examples.en: I never thought a village like this would really exist.
That hero is a figure who never actually existed.
Does an island that isn't on the map really exist?

explain: '있다'와 달리 '실제로 존재하는지'를 따질 때 써서 '실존 인물'처럼 사람이나 장소에 붙여요. '실존하지 않는다'는 지어낸 것이라는 뜻으로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '진짜로 있다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike 있다, 실존하다 is used when asking whether something truly exists, usually about people or places, as in '실존 인물'. '실존하지 않는다' often means something was made up. In casual talk people say '진짜로 있다'.

en: enter (a city or capital); arrive at a big stage

examples.en: The team arrived safely in Beijing yesterday.
When the army entered the city, people cheered.

examples.ko: 대표팀은 내일 경기가 열리는 도시에 입성해요.
examples.en: The national team arrives tomorrow in the city hosting the match.

examples.ko: 새 감독이 오늘 팀에 입성할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The new coach is set to join the team today.

examples.ko: 서울에 입성하는 날 비가 많이 왔어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot on the day I arrived in Seoul.

examples.ko: 시골에서 올라온 청년이 대도시에 입성하고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The young man who came up from the countryside was stunned on arriving in the big city.

explain: 성이나 도시 안으로 들어서는 큰 장면에 어울리는 말이에요. 요즘은 뉴스에서 선수단이나 가수가 새 도시나 팀에 도착할 때 많이 써요. 행사장 안으로 들어갈 때는 '입장하다'를 써서 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It fits a big scene of entering a walled city or capital. In today's news it's used when a team or singer arrives in a new city or joins a new team. For going into an event venue, use 입장하다 instead.

examples.ko: 올해 우리 가게의 판매 실적이 저조해요.
examples.en: Our shop's sales results are poor this year.
Turnout for the event was far too low.
I worry when my exam scores are poor.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 팀의 득점이 저조한 편이에요.
examples.en: Our team's scoring has been sluggish lately.
The response was weak, so we scaled down the event.

examples.ko: 출석이 저조하지 않도록 신경 써 주세요.
examples.en: Please make sure attendance doesn't turn out low.

explain: 성적, 실적, 참여율처럼 숫자로 보이는 결과가 기대보다 낮을 때 써요. 사람 자체를 가리키지 않고 '참여가 저조하다'처럼 일의 결과를 말해요. '부진하다'와 비슷한 상황에서 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: Used when a measurable result such as grades, performance, or turnout is lower than hoped. It describes the outcome of something, as in '참여가 저조하다', not a person. It's used in situations similar to 부진하다.

en: devote oneself to; concentrate wholly on

examples.en: These days I devote myself only to studying.
He quit his company to focus entirely on research.
Because of my child, I devoted myself to childcare for a while.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝날 때까지 준비에 전념할 거예요.
examples.en: I'll put all my effort into preparing until the exam is over.

examples.ko: 한 가지 일에 전념하는 사람이 멋있어요.
examples.en: A person who is devoted to one thing is cool.

examples.ko: 요즘 바빠서 일에 전념하지 못해서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm busy these days and can't focus fully on work, which worries me.

explain: '집중하다'는 한동안 한 가지에 주의를 모으는 것이고, '전념하다'는 다른 일은 접어 두고 한 가지에 시간과 힘을 쏟는 거예요. 그래서 '공부에 전념하다'처럼 오래 하는 일에 써요. 조사는 '~에'를 써요.
explain_en: 집중하다 is gathering your attention on one thing for a while; 전념하다 is putting aside other things and pouring your time and energy into one. So it suits long-term efforts like '공부에 전념하다', and the particle is 에.

examples.en: The company pushed ahead with the new construction as planned.
We'll go ahead with the event even if it rains.
The committee decided to force the vote through despite objections.
If you push through a schedule too hard, your health suffers.
They say the government is forcing the new policy through.

examples.ko: 피곤하면 강행하지 말고 하루 더 쉬어요.
examples.en: If you're tired, don't push on; rest one more day.

explain: 반대가 있거나 어려운 상황인데도 그대로 밀어붙이는 느낌이라 좋은 뜻으로는 잘 안 써요. '진행하다'는 그냥 이어서 하는 말이라 이런 느낌이 없어요. '공사를 강행하다', '출발을 강행하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of pressing on despite opposition or difficulty, so it isn't usually positive. 진행하다 just means carrying on and has no such edge. It takes an object, as in '공사를 강행하다' and '출발을 강행하다'.
